page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.1-16 is a flexible virtual machine instance powered by the 64-bit ARM architecture. It utilizes Ampere AmpereOne processors running at a sustained base frequency of 3.0 GHz. The instance configuration provisions 2 dedicated physical cores, corresponding to 2 vCPUs at a ratio of one thread per core. Because simultaneous multithreading is disabled by design, each core executes independently without hyperthreading contention. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, resulting in an 8.0 GB allocation per dedicated core.

Hardware acceleration and integrated disk resources are absent from this profile. The instance includes 0 GPUs and provides no local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent data and operating system installations rely on networked block storage volumes. For external network connectivity, the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address directly attached upon deployment.

With an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, VM.Standard.A2.Flex.1-16 is oriented toward memory-sensitive deployments that do not require wide multi-core scaling. The architecture delivers strong density and cost efficiency for dedicated ARM execution. It is suited for in-memory key-value caches, intermediate database engines, container host workers, microservices backends, and ARM-native continuous integration and build pipelines.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.1-16 is an ARM-based compute instance built on the Ampere AmpereOne processor family operating at 3.0 GHz. The virtual machine provision provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs with single-threaded execution, avoiding resource contention typical of simultaneous multithreading. Paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers a memory-dense ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The server includes no local disk storage and no GPU accelerators, necessitating remote block storage for persistent data. Designed as a flexible compute allocation with dedicated core isolation and a single included public IPv4 address, the VM.Standard.A2.Flex.1-16 is well structured for memory-oriented caching layers, small databases, containerized microservices, CI/CD runners, and ARM64 application development workloads.
